item.title: #003: Apartment Price Prediction in Polish Cities!
item.description:
Property Price Prediction Using XGBoost & Model Optimization

Business Objective: Developed a regression model to predict Apartment Price in order to support [business impact, e.g., pricing strategy, forecasting accuracy, operational decision-making].

Data & Feature Engineering:

Processed 122 873 records with 9 features. Key features: squareMeters, rooms, buildYear, collegeDistance, centreDistance, floorCount, poiCount, hasElevator, city.

Implemented:

  • rigorous EDA (distribution analysis, target leakage checks, feature–target relationships),
  • outlier treatment using box plots,
  • removed outliers using the IQR method to prevent extreme values from distorting model performance.,
  • feature transformations: new variables (‘age_of_building’) are created to enhance model performance, and categorical features are encoded,
  • multicollinearity diagnostics (correlation thresholds).

Modeling Strategy:

Established a comparative pipeline evaluating Linear Regression vs. XGBoost. Used GridSearchCV with cross-validation (k = 5) to systematically optimize key hyperparameters. Assessment focused on generalization performance, stability across folds, and error variance.

item.title: #002: 🚫 Don’t Do This in Excel!
item.description:
So you’ve discovered Power Query—welcome! 🌟 It’s like the Swiss Army knife for data: importing, cleaning, and transforming at the click of a button.

And at first, it’s amazing! But with that first taste of power, new users often get swept up, connecting to folders, stacking transformations like a pro… until chaos ensues. 🙈🙈🙈

If you’re not careful, you’ll end up with a messy web of queries that’s impossible to pass on, let alone move to a new file location.

item.title: #001: OIL TYPES PREDICTION
item.description:
Oil Analysis & Classification – Advanced End-to-End Machine Learning System

This project implements a complete analytical and predictive pipeline for industrial oil diagnostics using particle-count distributions, chemical composition, and ISO cleanliness measures. It demonstrates advanced data preprocessing, exploratory analysis, imbalanced learning, model optimization, feature selection, and interactive deployment through Streamlit. The goal is to classify oil samples into operational states (A, B, C, X) and provide interpretable, real-time predictions for maintenance engineers.
